The three exhaustive regions w<=u<=v, u<=w<=v, u<=v<=w give the sharp 1−P+r Pdot>=0 for p<=3; in the last region the bound reduces to (1−a)(2−a)>=0 with a=(u/v)^p. For an arbitrary unilateral deviation at distance h<R, linearly interpolate the two NUMERICAL distances, not metric points; triangle reverse inequality ensures 1-Lipschitz velocities. C(s)=s+(R−s)P(s) has derivative >=0, including nearest-neighbor switches by absolute continuity; h>=R and <=2 distinct reports are immediate boundary cases. A line at (−1,0,1+ε) yields limiting right derivative 2(3−p)/9<0 for each p>3. The closest-pair optimum equals a, and the exact welfare profile F_p(t)=(2+t^(p−1))/(2+t^p) is realized by (0,t,t+1); at p=3 its unique critical root solves t³+6t=4 and F_p decreases strictly with p for 0<t<1. Independently rebuilt 62,500 exact-rational four-point comparisons, a p=4 strict gain and cubic-root bracket. Bounded checks corroborate only finite cases, not universal claims.

value.rationale: The exponent p is an intrinsic continuous parameter in a natural randomized nearest-report-omission family.
